rules.title: Statewide prohibition on rent control
rules.requirement: Massachusetts law broadly prohibits any regulatory scheme based on or implementing rent control. Rent control is defined to include any regulation that in any way requires below-market rents for residential properties. No local rent cap is allowed.
rules.key_value: State bars rent control; no rent cap permitted

coverage.summary: Statewide bar on rent control for residential properties.

rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in the passages.
rules.quoted_span: General Laws c. 40P, § 2, "broadly prohibits any regulatory scheme based upon or implementing rent control."
rules.review_note: Described in an SJC opinion (Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893). The statute text itself is not in the passages.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 (statewide cap on annual rent increases)
rules.requirement: The petition would have repealed G.L. c. 40P and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of the CPI increase or 5%. The SJC held that art. 48 bars it from the November 2026 ballot because of its religious-facilities exemption.
rules.key_value: Cap: lesser of annual CPI increase or 5%

new_construction_exemption.basis: newly constructed units less than 10 years old

unverifiable_exemptions: dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes
coverage.summary: Statewide cap for most residential rental units. Exempts owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units under 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes.
coverage.owner_conditions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units exempt

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units; newly constructed units less than 10 years old; certain publicly regulated units; short-term rentals; dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or non-profit purposes.
rules.effective_date_note: Never took effect; barred from the November 2026 ballot.
citation_aliases: An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
rules.review_note: Exemption details come from a secondary source (passage p7) and are truncated. The SJC opinion (p1, p2) confirms the ballot bar.
rules.source_notes: The SJC opinion says art. 48 bars placement on the November 2026 ballot.
